questions: What does "replace each of A_i and A_{i+1}" mean in the context of modifying the sequence A?
Are the operations on indices performed modulo N to handle wraparound, or do they stop at index N?
Can the same operation be applied multiple times to overlapping triplets in a single step?
Is the initial sequence A fixed throughout all operations, or can it change during the process?
Does the problem require that at least one valid transformation sequence exists, or just that the string satisfies the condition at some point?
What constitutes a "good string" — must it allow reaching a specific state, or simply permit any number of operations without contradiction?
How should conflicting replacements (e.g., trying to set A_i to both 0 and 1) be handled?
Are duplicate characters allowed in constructing the string S, and how do they affect the operations?
answers: We replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with the value 1.
Only as given by the stated wraparound definitions (S_{N+1}=S_1, etc.).
Not specified beyond what's given; operations may be applied repeatedly, including to overlapping triplets.
A is initially the given input sequence and changes as operations are applied to it.
A good string is one for which some sequence of operations achieves the goal (A contains no 0); it need not be the case that every sequence works, just that one exists.
S is good if the operations can be performed any number of times so that A ends up containing no 0; not merely 'without contradiction'.
This can't arise, since every operation only ever sets values to 1, never to 0.
Not specified; nothing restricts S from containing duplicate characters.
inline_prompts: You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of length N, consisting of 0 and 1. We call a string S of length N, consisting only of uppercase English letters, a good string if it is possible to perform the following operation any number of times (possibly zero). Here, S_i (1\leq i\leq N) denotes the i-th character of S, and we define S_{N+1}=S_1, S_{N+2}=S_2, and A_{N+1}=A_1. - Perform one of the following operations: - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_i= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_{i+2}= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with the value 1. - Choose an integer i with 1\leq i\leq N such that S_{i+2}= A, S_{i+1}= R, and S_i= C, and replace each of A_i and A_{i+1} with 1. Determine whether there exists a good string. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output If there exists a good string, print Yes; otherwise, print No. The judge is case-insensitive; for example, if the correct answer is Yes, outputs such as yes, YES, or yEs will also be accepted. Constraints - 3\leq N\leq 200000 - A_i\in \lbrace 0,1 \rbrace (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
